newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak bank sees 97 profit static - agency.
newsitem.headline: Slovak bank sees 97 profit static - agency.

text.p: Slovak Prva Komunalna Banka (PKB) a.s. expects to post an after-tax profit of 160 million crowns in 1997, roughly equivalent to last year, the official news agency TASR reported on Tuesday.
Quoting PKB President Jozef Mihalik, TASR said the bank expects its 1997 pre-tax profit to total 180 million crowns, and its balance sheet to rise to 16 billion crowns from 13.37 billion in 1996.
He did not elaborate on its profits for 1996.
Mihalik said that though the bank was not considering a sizeable increase in its loan portfolio soon, it would continue to provide municipal loans to finance public sector investment.
In co-operation with the construction ministry, PKB will also co-finance public housing construction which should resume some time this year and end in the second half of 1998, he said.
Zilina-based PKB, is a three-year old private universal bank -- Slovakia's ninth largest bank -- specialising mainly in providing services to the municipal sector.
Mihalik added that "decisive" shareholders of the bank are municipalities.

PKB carries a BB+ senior debt rating by Thomson BankWatch, which it was assigned last month. Thomson has also assigned PKB with an LC-2 short-term local currency debt rating to PKB, saying the bank has been showing favourable financial trends and success as a "niche player".
